bds.h: LeBlanc fields questions about trade negotiations with Trump administration
bds.lede: Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc maintained Tuesday that Prime Minister Mark Carney’s version of the events leading up to the collapse of U.S. trade talks was accurate as he was questioned by members of Parliament in Ottawa.
rows: Prime Minister Carney downplayed US concerns on Wednesday, saying its ties are not a "top issue" for President Trump as Canada eyes trade with Chinese carmakers.

Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc maintained Tuesday that Prime Minister Mark Carney’s version of the events leading up to the collapse of U.S. trade talks was accurate as he was questioned by members of Parliament in Ottawa.

SHENZHEN — Mark Carney met with U.S. President Donald Trump in China on a day when the prime minister noted trade talks with Washington are far more complex than the ones Canada is having with Beijing.

Prime Minister Mark Carney, speaking from China on Nov. 18, said Canada and the U.S. have different types of trade relationships with Beijing, adding that in the 'hierarchy of issues' between Canada and the U.S., China is not 'the top issue at all.'
Carney and Trump discussed “the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement,” according to an official readout from the Canadian side.
